title: Observability gateway: tenant throttling and opaque trace headers for Dedicated/Private
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Build a new on-prem/ VPC-scoped Observability Gateway that centralizes ingest for Dedicated and Private deployments and enforces tenant-level quotas, adaptive throttling, and opaque trace header injection. Goal is to provide strong tenant isolation for traces/metrics/logs without sacrificing traceability inside a tenant, enable predictable cost controls for Dedicated customers, and avoid accidental cross-tenant trace exposure in shared collection layers. This gateway will sit at the cluster perimeter (or on a small dedicated VM for air-gapped installs) and forward validated events into existing backend pipelines (OTLP, Prometheus remote write, and a Kafka/ingest buffer).

Key goals: 
- Per-tenant ingest accounting and soft/hard quotas for tokens/events.
- Adaptive throttling that favors latency SLOs for foreground traffic while shedding background telemetry when overloaded.
- Opaque trace header scheme: convert incoming trace IDs to tenant-scoped opaque IDs and maintain reversible mapping inside the gateway for allowed debug sessions. Prevent raw customer trace IDs from being usable to enumerate or link across tenants.
- Local encrypted buffering for offline/on-prem scenarios with configurable retention and backpressure signals.
- Schema validation and enrichment: enforce tag/label allowlist, redact PII heuristics, and normalize log/metric schemas to reduce downstream noise.
- Expose per-tenant observability into Redwood Console (per-tenant ingress rate, quota usage, recent throttling events, top error buckets).
acceptance_criteria: Gateway deployable to Dedicated clusters and to a single-VM package for on-prem airgapped installs
Per-tenant quotas implemented with soft-warning and hard-drop policies and configurable by admin
Opaque trace header generated for each incoming span and mapping persisted only in gateway KV with TTL; samples traceable when tenant authorizes gateway debug token
Schema validation rejects malformed OTLP and rejects disallowed tag keys with a clear rejection metric
Encrypted local buffer honors retention and exposes backpressure via 429 and service-level health signals
Console dashboard shows per-tenant ingress, throttling events, and 95th/99th latency with links to example spans/logs
implementation_notes: Gateway will be implemented as a lightweight Go service using existing OTLP ingestion libraries; existing collector code can be reused for parsing/validation
Use Redis (or embedded RocksDB for single-VM) to store opaque trace ID mappings with HMAC-rotating keys per-tenant
Throttling algorithm: token-bucket per-tenant plus global adaptive shedder based on 95th latency and queue length
Local buffer encryption: AES-256-GCM using node KMS; integration with customer KMS optional for Private installs
Integrate metrics via Prometheus remote_write to the same metrics pipeline; expose internal metrics with tenant label when allowed
PII detection uses a lightweight heuristic engine (email/ssn patterns) and a redact-on-write policy configurable per-customer
rollout_plan: 1) feature-flagged internal dogfood in staging (1/cluster) with conservative quotas; 2) invite-only Early Access with three Dedicated customers for 2 weeks; 3) gradual ramp with per-customer quota tuning and 24/7 oncall for first 72h; 4) default enable for new Dedicated clusters, opt-in for existing customers until 2026-06
test_plan: Unit tests for trace mapping and reverse-resolution logic
Load tests simulating 100 tenants with skewed traffic (10% tenants produce 90% load)
Chaos test: disconnect backend for 30m and validate local buffer retention and recovery
Security test: ensure opaque trace IDs cannot be used to correlate across tenant boundaries
E2E: sample tenant pipelines through gateway into Console dashboards with simulated errors and validate alerting
